summary: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin 38.1.6 ships preinstall dropper that executes obfuscated Bun payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs checks for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads a Bun release archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/..., extracts it to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file `math_init.js` at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB Bun-CJS module (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) that is heavily obfuscated (shuffled string-array with a `WV8StW` rotation decoder) and is not listed in package.json `files` (which declares only `dist` and `src`), so it is smuggled into the tarball outside the declared file manifest. The legitimate ESLint rules under dist/ and src/ are not referenced by the preinstall path — the dropper and obfuscated payload are wholly unrelated to the package's stated ESLint-plugin purpose. On `npm install`, the preinstall hook fires automatically and executes the obfuscated Bun payload with full user privileges, using an alternate runtime specifically to evade Node-based static analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
